description:
# Package + publish spendbar 0.1

## Hard rule: no autonomous publish

**This ticket must never be executed without the user's explicit, in-session go-ahead for the publish itself.** Publishing to npm is irreversible and outward-facing (metadata is mirrored widely; a shipped identifier is permanent). Handover `2026-07-31-03-auto-session.md` records this as a deliberate exclusion: "T-007 (`npm publish`) must not be started autonomously." Ticket assignment, a green test suite, or plan approval are NOT consent — only a direct user instruction authorizing `npm publish` of this specific version is. Everything up to but excluding `npm publish` (scrubs, tests, dry-runs, tarball audits) may be prepared; the publish command itself waits.

## Why this ticket exists

Final step of v0.1 in `product-architecture-2026-07-30.md` (Phases table, v0.1 row): "`npm pack` tarball test; script-disabled install tests: npm + pnpm + yarn + bun install the packed tarball with lifecycle scripts disabled and run the CLI + pinned ccusage (round-3 — v0.1 publishes, so v0.1 proves installability); publish. Exit: parity harness green; all four package managers install + run clean." T-003–T-006 are complete (handover 2026-07-31-03): `npm run test:all` = 314 unit tests, contract 16/16, parity `--final` 266/0/0, 45/45 goldens byte-match. This is the only remaining v0.1 ticket.

npm context (handover 2026-07-31-01): `spendbar@0.0.2` is LIVE from the owner's `<owner-npm-account>` account; 0.0.1 was **unpublished because it carried an author field** — the owner explicitly wants no personal-name attribution, ever. The storybloq npm org has team read-write on `spendbar`; `@storybloq/spendbar` deliberately unclaimed; maintainers sidebar still shows `<owner-npm-account>` (fix needs a brand account — owner action).

## Current state (verified 2026-07-31, branch v0.1-ts-port)

- `package.json`: name `spendbar`, version `0.1.0-dev`, `bin: {spendbar: dist/cli.js}`, `files: [dist, README.md]`, `engines: node >=22.12.0`, ccusage pinned exact `20.0.19` as a regular dependency, **no author field**, no `repository`/`homepage`/`bugs`. `prepack`+`prepare` run the build (pack-time/dev-side only — consumers installing from the registry never execute a dependency's `prepare`; there are no install-time scripts, satisfying the plan's zero-lifecycle-scripts constraint).
- `tests-ts/contract/packaging.contract.mjs` already covers most of the original ticket body: builds a REAL `npm pack` tarball, asserts the bin exists with shebang + executable mode (backed by `scripts/postbuild.mjs`), asserts no `.jsonl`/tests/spikes/scripts/.story paths ship, asserts only `dist/` + `package.json`/`README.md`/`LICENSE`, installs the exact tarball into a scratch prefix, and smoke-tests `--help` (exit 0, `usage: spendbar [-h]`) and the exit-2 stderr error path.
- The attribution test to cite precisely — `packaging.contract.mjs:111-119`, test "carries no personal attribution": asserts `MANIFEST[field] === undefined` for each of `author`, `contributors`, `maintainers`, then `assert.doesNotMatch(JSON.stringify(MANIFEST), /<maintainer-name>/i, "personal name found in package.json")`. **Blind spot: it greps only package.json, not tarball file contents** — see gate 2 below.

## Pre-publish gates (must be done, in order)

1. **ISS-005 scrub**: the real Codex rollout ID `rollout-2026-07-09T00-43-18-<session id removed — T-024>` (verified: a genuine session on the author's machine) is still at `src/codex.ts:30` and compiles into `dist/codex.js:28` — tsc keeps comments, so it ships in the tarball. Replace with the synthetic-UUIDv7 convention the fixtures use (real timestamp prefix + all-zero random bits, e.g. `...-<session id removed — T-024>`). Note ISS-005 also names `usage.py:199` and `product-architecture-2026-07-30.md:10` — neither ships, and usage.py is the frozen oracle: owner decision, see openQuestions.
2. **Newly found, same class**: `src/context.ts:141-142` (→ `dist/context.js:80-81`, ships) carries the maintainer's username and real home path (`USER=<real-account>`, `/Users/testuser/.codex`) in a comment. Scrub to a synthetic user, then **extend the packaging contract test so the `/<maintainer-name>/i` (plus `<real-account>` and local-rollout-ID pattern) grep runs over the unpacked tarball's file contents, not just the manifest** — that closes the blind spot that let this through 16 green contract tests.
3. **High-severity parity issues, tracker hygiene**: ISS-006/ISS-009 (encodePath astral split), ISS-012 (UTF-16-unit ordering) and the medium ISS-007/ISS-010 (padding) appear FIXED in source — `src/config.ts:20` now has the `u` flag, `src/pysort.ts` implements code-point ordering used by aggregate/renderers, `src/format.ts` pads via `pyLen` — but all remain OPEN in the tracker. Before publish: verify each fix has differential-test coverage, and resolve the issues (or record an owner waiver). Do not publish with high-severity parity issues open-and-unexplained.
4. **ISS-013/ISS-014 decision** (Windows `~` expansion uses POSIX semantics; `ntpath.expanduser` differs; ALLOWLIST entry 17 records it as a KNOWN GAP, explicitly NOT a sanctioned delta, while README's platform table advertises Windows x64+arm64): owner must pick — fix, caveat the README, or drop the Windows claim for 0.1.0. See openQuestions; a README caveat is the cheap default but it changes an advertised platform claim, so it is not an autonomous call.
5. **README rewrite for npm**: `README.md` ships in the tarball and becomes the npm page, but it is still the Python tool's README — titled "usage", install = clone + symlink `usage.py`, bin name `usage`, a `github.com/<your-username>` placeholder, and an intro paragraph describing per-run `npx` fetching that the port deliberately does not do (the `### ccusage` section already describes the port's pinned-dependency behavior — the rest doesn't). Minimum: spendbar name, `npm install -g spendbar`, `spendbar` subcommand synopsis, keep the accuracy/caveats and acknowledgements sections, no personal identifiers.

## Publish checklist (after gates, after explicit go-ahead)

- Version: bump `0.1.0-dev` → `0.1.0` (publishing moves the `latest` dist-tag off 0.0.2 — intended, confirm with owner).
- `npm run test:all` green at the publish commit (unit + both Python suites + contract + parity `--final` + goldens).
- Script-disabled install matrix (plan v0.1 exit criterion, currently NOT met — only npm, without `--ignore-scripts`): npm, pnpm, yarn, bun each install the exact packed tarball with lifecycle scripts disabled (`--ignore-scripts` / manager equivalent) into a clean prefix; run `spendbar --help` and one invocation proving the **pinned ccusage resolves offline** (exercise `dist/resolve-ccusage.js` path — no network, no npx). Script it so it is re-runnable.
- `npm pack --dry-run` + unpack audit: file list matches the contract-test allowlist exactly; grep unpacked contents for `<maintainer-name>`, `<real-account>`, `/Users/`, and the rollout-ID pattern; check no sourcemaps/`.d.ts`/stray files; record tarball size.
- `npm publish --dry-run` from the release commit; inspect what npm says it will send (manifest, files, size).
- Auth: publish requires the `<owner-npm-account>` account with 2FA/OTP (or an owner-created brand account — openQuestion). **Provenance (`--provenance`) is NOT attainable for 0.1.0**: it requires publishing from supported CI, and this repo has no CI (handover 2026-07-31-03). Flag, don't fake.
- `repository` field: currently absent; npm will warn. Decision needed — see openQuestions (a personal GitHub URL would put `<maintainer-name>` in the manifest and FAIL packaging.contract.mjs:118's grep, so this is not a fill-in-the-blank).
- After publish: `npm view spendbar@0.1.0` — confirm version, files count, shasum, absence of `author`; install from the REGISTRY (not the local tarball) into a throwaway prefix and run `spendbar --help`; confirm the npm page renders the new README.
- Tag `v0.1.0` on the published commit; record tarball shasum in the release note/handover.

## Out of scope

MCP server, service, menubar (v0.2+); `@spendbar`/`@storybloq` scope claims; brand npm account creation (owner action); CI/trusted-publishing setup (flag it, don't build it here); fixing usage.py (frozen oracle); non-gating issues below.

## Ship-in-0.1.x (judged non-gating)

ISS-001/ISS-003 (stderr truncation slices UTF-16 units — error-path cosmetic), ISS-002/ISS-004 (`blocks --json` schema validation gap), ISS-015 (`.trim()` vs `str.strip()` — 5 error-message divergences), ISS-016 (JS ASCII `\d` vs Python Unicode `\d` — requires non-ASCII digits in machine-generated rollout filenames; unrealistic input), ISS-017 (usage.py oracle bug, frozen), ISS-018–ISS-021 (harness follow-ups: fixture artifacts, TS replayer, allowlist execution evidence, fixture-schema CASES).

## Constraints (standing, all verified against repo/handovers)

- `usage.py` is the frozen oracle — never modified (scrubbing its line 199 needs an explicit owner exemption).
- `package.json` must never carry `author`/`contributors`/`maintainers` or the maintainer's name (enforced by packaging.contract.mjs:111-119; 0.0.1 was unpublished over exactly this).
- No real transcript data, session identifiers, or personal paths in fixtures OR anything that ships (contract test blocks `.jsonl` and test dirs at the tarball boundary; extend to content grep per gate 2).
- Zero install-time lifecycle scripts in the published package.
- `engines: node >=22.12.0` (already present; keep).

## Acceptance criteria
1. The session transcript contains an explicit user message authorizing `npm publish` of spendbar 0.1.0 BEFORE any publish command is run; no publish command appears without it.
2. Unpacking the `npm pack` tarball and running `grep -riE '<maintainer-name>|<real-account>|<session id removed — T-024>' .` over its contents returns no matches except (pending the LICENSE openQuestion) the LICENSE copyright line; specifically the rollout ID formerly at src/codex.ts:30 and the username/home path formerly at src/context.ts:141-142 no longer appear in dist/.
3. tests-ts/contract/packaging.contract.mjs is extended so the personal-attribution assertion covers unpacked tarball file contents (not only JSON.stringify of package.json), and `npm run test:contract` passes including the 'carries no personal attribution' test.
4. A re-runnable script installs the exact packed tarball with lifecycle scripts disabled under npm, pnpm, yarn, and bun into clean prefixes; in each, `spendbar --help` exits 0 printing `usage: spendbar [-h]`, and one invocation proves the pinned ccusage 20.0.19 resolves with no network access; all four pass.
5. package.json at the publish commit has name `spendbar`, version `0.1.0` (no -dev suffix), engines node >=22.12.0, ccusage pinned exactly (no ^/~), no author/contributors/maintainers field, and no preinstall/install/postinstall scripts.
6. `npm run test:all` is green at the publish commit (all unit tests, both Python suites, contract suite, parity --final with 0 failures/0 skips, all goldens matching).
7. ISS-005, ISS-006, ISS-009, and ISS-012 are resolved in the tracker (or carry a recorded owner waiver) before publish; the ISS-013/ISS-014 Windows decision and the README platform table are consistent with each other.
8. README.md in the tarball describes the npm package: installs via `npm install -g spendbar`, names the bin `spendbar`, contains no clone-and-symlink-usage.py install path, no `<your-username>` placeholder, and no personal identifiers.
9. After publish: `npm view spendbar@0.1.0` shows the expected version and file count with no author field; `npm install -g spendbar@0.1.0` into a throwaway prefix succeeds and `spendbar --help` exits 0; a git tag `v0.1.0` exists on the published commit.

## Risks
Publish is the point of no return: anything in the tarball (the ISS-005 rollout ID in dist/codex.js:28, the maintainer's username in dist/context.js:80-81) becomes permanently mirrored npm metadata/content — and the current contract suite passes with both present, because the attribution grep only reads package.json. Secondary risks: the shipped README currently misdescribes the package (Python install path, npx claims) and would become the public npm page; the Windows support claim contradicts a documented known gap (ISS-013/014); publishing moves `latest` off 0.0.2 for all installers immediately; adding a repository field carelessly re-introduces the personal name the owner unpublished 0.0.1 over; provenance cannot be attested without CI, so skipping it must be a recorded decision rather than an oversight; and the tracker still shows ISS-006/009/012 open even though the fixes exist in source, so publishing without reconciling tracker vs code risks shipping with an unverified fix or re-litigating solved problems in 0.1.x.

## Open questions (owner decisions)
1. LICENSE says 'Copyright (c) 2026 <maintainer name>' and npm always ships LICENSE regardless of the files allowlist — does the no-personal-attribution requirement extend to the license copyright holder (e.g. reassign to 'spendbar contributors' or the storybloq org), or does legal clarity win? MIT needs a named holder; only the owner can decide.
2. repository/homepage/bugs fields: absent today. A personal GitHub URL would embed '<maintainer-name>' in the manifest and fail the contract test's grep. Point them at a storybloq-org repo, or omit entirely for 0.1.0?
3. ISS-005 residue outside the tarball: usage.py:199 (frozen oracle — modification needs an explicit exemption plus a parity re-run) and product-architecture-2026-07-30.md:10 (absolute home path + Claude session UUID) carry the same class of identifier in the public repo. Scrub with exemption, or accept repo-side residue since neither ships?
4. ISS-013/ISS-014: Windows ~ expansion is a documented known gap while README advertises Windows x64+arm64. For 0.1.0 — implement ntpath semantics (unverifiable here, no Windows reference interpreter), add a README caveat, or drop the Windows row?
5. Publish identity: publish from <owner-npm-account> (2FA/OTP at hand?) or create the storybloq-bot brand account first (also fixes the maintainers-sidebar residue)? And is deferring npm provenance acceptable given there is no CI, or should GitHub Actions trusted publishing be set up before 0.1.0?
6. Confirm: publishing 0.1.0 moves the `latest` dist-tag off 0.0.2 — intended? Should v0.1-ts-port merge to main before publish, or is publishing from the branch with a v0.1.0 tag acceptable?
7. package.json description and keywords promise 'MCP server and native macOS menubar' which 0.1 does not ship — keep as a roadmap statement on the npm page or trim to what 0.1.0 actually delivers?

**Related issues:** ISS-005, ISS-006, ISS-007, ISS-009, ISS-010, ISS-012, ISS-013, ISS-014, ISS-001, ISS-002, ISS-015, ISS-016, ISS-017
title: Package + publish spendbar 0.1
